frequency_question: How often does major federal voting legislation fail to pass the U.S. Senate due to procedural friction (the 60-vote filibuster threshold) within a given Congress?
membership_rule: Includes major partisan electoral reform bills (e.g., Freedom to Vote Act, For the People Act, SAVE Act iterations) that required 60 votes to overcome procedural blocks. Excludes unanimous consent resolutions and non-controversial technical corrections.

cases.name: National Voter Registration Act amendments / various voter ID push bills (1996-2004)
Help America Vote Act (2002 - passed, but distinct bipartisan consensus)
DISCLOSE Act / Fair Elections Now Act (2010)
Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act (2022)

coverage_note: 5 major legislative vehicles identified representing high-friction partisan voting bills over three decades.
known_gaps: Excludes minor committee-level amendments that never reached formal floor cloture votes.
skeleton: Major partisan election bills subjected to Senate filibuster: 5 major attempts identified where party-line voter eligibility/reform measures were brought to a test; 4 failed to pass the Senate due to the 60-vote threshold, and 1 passed via rare bipartisan consensus (HAVA 2002). For strictly partisan voter eligibility/ID bills, failure rate is 4 out of 4.
multiplier: 4 misses out of 5 major attempts (80% failure rate for general class, 100% failure rate for partisan-only subset).
validity_reason: Senate filibuster rules and polarization dynamics remain stable over this horizon.
